title: LRU cache with deterministic TTL expiry
instructions:
Complete `cache_entry.py` and `lru_cache.py`. Export dataclass `cache_entry.Entry(value: object, expires_at: float | None)` and `Entry.expired(now: float) -> bool`, true exactly when expires_at is not None and now >= expires_at.

Export `lru_cache.LRUCache(capacity: int, clock: Callable[[], float])`. Capacity must be a positive non-boolean integer or raise `ValueError`. The supplied clock returns finite seconds, monotonically nondecreasing; never use a real clock. Keys are strings and values arbitrary objects. Operations below obtain one clock reading per call and remove ALL expired entries before doing their work (except that invalid put TTLs are rejected before reading the clock or changing state).
- `put(key: str, value: object, ttl: float | None = None) -> None`: None means no expiry. A TTL must be a finite, nonnegative int or float (booleans excluded), otherwise `ValueError`. For positive TTL, expiry is now + ttl. TTL zero removes an existing key and stores nothing. An insert or replacement makes the key most recently used and replaces its prior expiry. If the cache exceeds capacity, evict least recently used live keys until it fits.
- `get(key: str, default=None) -> object`: return the stored value and move a found key to most recent; otherwise return the exact default object.
- `delete(key: str) -> bool`: remove a live key and return True; return False if missing/expired.
- `keys() -> list[str]`: return a fresh list of live keys from least to most recent; inspecting keys does not change recency.
- `__len__() -> int`: count live entries without changing recency.

Missing gets/deletes never alter live-key recency. At exactly the expiry time an entry is expired. Instances are independent. Implement expiry logic in Entry and use it in the cache; no background work or sleeping.

- `cache_entry.py`
- `lru_cache.py`
